reviewBoundary: These are review-ready drafts, not verified publication chapters. No machine setting, safety procedure, or material processing value may be inferred from them.

sourceSeeds.title: Plastics — Injection moulding of test specimens of thermoplastic materials — Part 1: General principles, and moulding of multipurpose and bar test specimens
sourceSeeds.scope: General injection-moulding principles, consistent process-parameter descriptions and reproducible reporting. ISO confirms the 2017 edition remains current after review in 2022.

chapters.applicability: General thermoplastic injection-moulding concepts only. Actual process windows depend on the material grade, machine, mould, part requirements and applicable site controls.

sections.title: The process in one sentence
sections.text: Injection moulding repeatedly prepares a polymer melt, drives a controlled quantity into a closed mould, allows the material to form and solidify sufficiently, and removes the moulded part so the cycle can repeat.

sections.title: What the process must achieve
sections.text: A useful process must do more than fill the visible cavity. It must produce the required geometry and properties with repeatable conditions, while staying inside the limits of the material, machine, mould and safety system.

sections.title: Why settings are not universal
sections.text: Moulding conditions are not transferable constants. Standards for reproducible test-specimen moulding explicitly recognise that required conditions vary with the material. Production parts add further dependence on geometry, mould design, machine capability and quality requirements.

sections.title: How to think like a process engineer
sections.text: Separate the desired part result from the machine inputs used to create it. Observe what the material and cavity are doing, record the conditions that matter, and change one justified variable at a time when establishing cause and effect.

chapters.applicability: Conceptual cycle model. Controller names, available phases and transition methods vary by machine and process.

sections.title: Prepare the next shot
sections.text: The plasticising unit rotates and retracts the screw to prepare a controlled quantity of melt for a later injection. Material preparation and thermal history continue to matter even when the mould is closed and cooling.

sections.title: Fill the cavity
sections.text: The machine advances the screw so melt flows through the nozzle, feed system and gate into the cavity. During this phase, flow resistance and the commanded motion interact; displayed hydraulic or injection pressure is not itself proof of cavity pressure.

sections.title: Transfer and pack
sections.text: A controlled transition moves the process from filling toward post-fill pressure control. Packing compensates for material contraction while the gate and part remain able to respond. The correct transition and packing strategy must be established for the actual moulded system rather than copied as a universal percentage or pressure.

sections.title: Cool and eject
sections.text: The part must remain constrained long enough to reach a condition where opening and ejection can occur without unacceptable deformation or damage. Cooling, mould temperature distribution, part geometry and material behaviour all affect this stage.

sections.title: Treat the cycle as an interacting system
sections.text: Cycle phases overlap physically even when the controller displays them separately. Plasticising may occur while the part cools, and thermal or pressure history from one phase can change what happens in the next. Diagnose the complete sequence, not a single screen value in isolation.

chapters.applicability: General injection-moulding-machine architecture. Exact guarding, drives, controls and component names depend on the machine manufacturer and configuration.

sections.title: Injection unit
sections.text: The injection unit receives material, plasticises it, meters the shot and drives melt toward the mould. Common functional elements include the feed system, heated barrel, reciprocating screw, non-return function and nozzle, but their designs and control methods vary.

sections.title: Clamping unit
sections.text: The clamping unit supports the mould, closes it, provides the required closing and clamping functions, opens it after the moulding phase and supports ejection-related motion. Machine architecture can be hydraulic, electric or hybrid and may use different mechanical arrangements.

sections.title: Control and energy systems
sections.text: The controller coordinates commanded motion, temperatures, pressures, timing, alarms and interlocks. The machine also contains energy sources and stored-energy hazards that cannot be understood safely from the process screen alone.

sections.title: Use the machine documentation
sections.text: For setup, maintenance, guarding, isolation, limits and permitted operation, the specific machine manufacturer's instructions and the site's approved procedures control. A generic Book chapter cannot replace them.

chapters.applicability: General mould-component concepts and terminology. Actual mould construction varies widely and may omit or add systems described here.

sections.title: The mould creates the part-forming space
sections.text: Core and cavity surfaces define the moulded geometry. The mould also has to receive melt, remove heat, separate in a controlled way and release the part without damaging the component or tooling.

sections.title: Feed system
sections.text: A conventional feed path may include a sprue, runners and gates. Hot-runner systems change how melt is conveyed and controlled. The gate is both a flow restriction and a process boundary, so its geometry and thermal state can strongly affect filling and post-fill behaviour.

sections.title: Guidance, support and ejection
sections.text: Mould assemblies use locating, guiding and supporting components to maintain alignment and carry loads. Ejection systems then apply controlled motion to release the moulding. The exact component arrangement must be identified from the real tool rather than assumed from a generic diagram.

sections.title: Temperature-control system
sections.text: Cooling or temperature-control circuits remove or supply heat so the mould reaches a useful thermal condition. Circuit layout, flow condition and local heat load can create different surface temperatures across the tool, which is why a single controller setpoint does not describe the whole mould.

chapters.applicability: Awareness only. It is not a lockout/tagout procedure, machine-specific safe system of work, guarding instruction or authorisation to enter a hazardous area.

sections.title: Safety is a system boundary
sections.text: Injection-moulding equipment combines hazardous motion, hot surfaces and materials, pressure, electrical energy and other machine-dependent energy sources. Safe work depends on engineered safeguards, correct machine condition, authorised procedures and competent people.

sections.title: A stopped screen is not an isolation
sections.text: The absence of commanded movement does not prove that hazardous energy has been isolated or dissipated. Never infer a safe intervention state from a controller display, cycle stop or open guard alone.

sections.title: Guarding and interlocks are safety functions
sections.text: Do not defeat, bypass or treat safeguards as production inconveniences. If a safeguard prevents the intended task, the task needs the approved machine- and site-specific safe method rather than an improvised workaround.

sections.title: When this Book must stop
sections.text: If a task involves access to a danger zone, isolation, stored energy, maintenance, abnormal machine condition or uncertainty about a safeguard, this Book does not provide the procedure. Use the machine manufacturer's instructions, the site's authorised safety system and competent supervision.
